message.content:
You are the implementer subagent for Task 5 of the VDA 5050 fleet adapter plan.

Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-20-vda5050-fleet-adapter.md (Task 5)
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/vda5050_fleet_adapter.md (§5 通信容灾与多车安全防撞安全准则)
Repo: /home/ubuntu/个人学习/amr_dispatcher, branch feat/vda5050-fleet-adapter

## Task Goal (P3): 逐段路权动态释放与断链安全守卫

Two rules from spec §5:
- **Rule 1 (动态解锁)**: When the vehicle's `state` report shows `lastNodeId` has advanced past node_A onto edge_AB (or further), automatically release the route locks the vehicle has LEFT BEHIND (its own trailing node/edge locks), waking waiting followers.
- **Rule 2 (断链安全)**: When the vehicle goes offline (connection LWT / heartbeat timeout), RETAIN all locks it holds — never release. Block new dispatch to it, log a watchdog warning. Locks are only reclaimed by: vehicle coming back online and re-verifying position, or operator manual force-release (manual force-release is out of scope — just log the guidance).

## Files
- Modify: `src/amr_dispatcher_core/src/workflow/traffic_planning.cpp` (or add a new pure-core helper header/cpp under `src/amr_dispatcher_core/include|src/workflow/` if cleaner — the unlock-decision logic must live in core, unit-testable, zero ROS)
- Modify: `src/amr_dispatcher_ros/src/dispatcher_node.cpp` (wire VDA 5050 state/online feeds into the core logic)
- Create: `test/unit/test_dynamic_unlocking.cpp`

## Prior Art you MUST read first
1. `src/amr_dispatcher_core/include/amr_dispatcher_core/dispatcher/traffic_reservation.hpp` + `src/dispatcher/traffic_reservation.cpp` — `ResourceTable` API: `Reserve`, `BuildLockIds`, `RouteNodeId`, `RouteEdgeId`, release/force-release methods (find exact names), owner tracking.
2. `src/amr_dispatcher_core/include/amr_dispatcher_core/workflow/traffic_planning.hpp` + `src/workflow/traffic_planning.cpp` — `PlanMissionRouteLocks` (forces include_intersection_locks=true — RULING: wiring must go through this or equivalent; `StationTransportRequest::traffic_intersection_locks_enabled` default false would yield all-Horizon orders, vehicle never moves).
3. `src/amr_dispatcher_ros/src/dispatcher_node.cpp` — how locks/missions currently flow; where VDA 5050 feeds should be subscribed.
4. `src/amr_dispatcher_ros/src/vda5050_gateway_node.cpp` (Task 4) — ROS-side contract you consume:
   - `/fleet/{vid}/state` — std_msgs/String with RAW VDA 5050 JSON → call `amr_dispatcher_core::fleet::DeserializeVda5050State` in dispatcher_node to extract fields (esp. `lastNodeId`, `lastNodeSequenceId`, `orderId`, `online`).
   - `/fleet/{vid}/online` — std_msgs/Bool, transient_local. false = LWT CONNECTIONBROKEN.
   - Gateway never touches locks — that's YOU (Task 5).
5. `src/amr_dispatcher_core/include/amr_dispatcher_core/fleet/vehicle_adapter_interface.hpp` — `VehicleStateReport`.
6. `src/amr_dispatcher_core/include/amr_dispatcher_core/fleet/vda5050_order_builder.hpp` — how released flags/order built; edge ids are `route_edge:A__B` (lexicographic, via ResourceTable statics). RULING: wire-level edgeId keeps this form; Task 5 back-parses via ResourceTable statics only.

## Design requirements for Rule 1 (dynamic unlocking)
- Pure-core function, e.g.:
  ```cpp
  // Returns lock ids (route_node:/route_edge:) that are now safe to release
  // given the vehicle's confirmed progress along its own order path.
  std::vector<std::string> ComputeTrailingLocksToRelease(
      const std::vector<std::string>& order_path_node_ids,
      const std::string& confirmed_last_node_id,
      uint32_t confirmed_last_node_sequence_id,
      /* any ownership filter inputs */);
  ```
  Exact signature is yours; requirements:
  - Only releases locks strictly BEHIND the confirmed position: everything up to and including the edge the vehicle has entered, plus nodes it has departed. Keep the node the vehicle is CURRENTLY ON plus the edge it is currently traversing LOCKED (physical footprint). Look at how `VehicleOrder` sequence_id works: nodes are even (i*2), edges occupy the odd slot between. If lastNodeId = path[k], the vehicle has physically passed nodes path[0..k-1] and edges between — release those; keep node path[k], edge (k→k+1), and everything ahead.
  - Conservative on ambiguity: unknown lastNodeId / sequence mismatch with order → release NOTHING (return empty), log guidance.
  - Idempotent: recomputing on repeated reports yields no re-release of already-released locks (ResourceTable release of non-held must be safe no-op — verify).
- Ownership safety: only locks whose owner is THIS mission/vehicle may be released. Read ResourceTable's owner fields and filter. Never release another vehicle's locks.

## Design requirements for Rule 2 (disconnect guard)
- Dispatcher subscribes `/fleet/{vid}/online`; on false: mark vehicle offline in dispatcher state, do NOT call any release, emit WARN log with spec-quoted guidance (仅发布 online=false，绝不释放路权锁...), and block new dispatches to that vehicle until online=true again.
- Also treat state-report staleness (no state for N seconds while online) as suspect: WARN but still do NOT release (per iron rule, only explicit progress releases locks).

## TDD
1. Write `test/unit/test_dynamic_unlocking.cpp` FIRST, confirm red (symbols missing):
   - Test: vehicle at path[0] → nothing released.
   - Test: vehicle advanced to path[1] → path[0] node lock + edge(0→1)... wait — vehicle ON edge(0→1) means edge is currently traversed → edge stays locked; node path[0] released. Advance to path[2] → node path[0], edge(0→1), node path[1]... verify against your design decision and document it in the test names (be explicit about the footprint rule: node currently occupied + edge currently traversed remain locked).
   - Test: unknown lastNodeId → empty release set.
   - Test: locks owned by a different mission are never returned for release.
   - Test: idempotency — compute twice, second call yields only still-held leftovers (or empty).
   - Test: Rule 2 guard — a pure-core helper like `ShouldRetainLocksForOfflineVehicle(...)` returning true always for offline, or dispatcher-level logic if pure-core form is artificial; if dispatcher-level only, cover the core pieces you can and state honestly what's only integration-tested.
2. Red → implement → green: `ctest --test-dir build/core` must go 591 → (591 + N) all passing.
3. Wire into `dispatcher_node.cpp`: subscribe state + online topics (create subscriptions when vehicle discovered — gateway creates /fleet/* lazily; use topic-inference or a parameter list of vehicles; simplest robust approach: subscribe with a wildcard is NOT available in ROS 2 — options: (a) parameter `vda5050_vehicles` list, (b) create subscriptions on discovery via detected missions. Pick the simplest that works with Task 4's lazy topic creation and document it).
4. Container colcon build: `docker exec amr_dispatcher bash -c "source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash && cd /workspace && colcon build --packages-select amr_dispatcher_ros --base-paths src"` (NOTE: this exact command works; plain --packages-select from /workspace fails package discovery).
5. Commit: `feat(core): 逐段路权动态释放与断链锁保留安全守卫` with trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>`

## Report back
Files touched, commit SHA, test count before/after, red-light evidence, design decision on footprint rule (which locks stay held at each progress point), container build result, concerns for Task 6.

tools.description:
Executes a given bash command and returns its output.

The working directory persists between commands, but shell state does not. The shell environment is initialized from the user's profile (bash or zsh).

IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user:

 - Read files: Use Read (NOT cat/head/tail)
 - Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)
 - Write files: Use Write (NOT echo >/cat <<EOF)
 - Communication: Output text directly (NOT echo/printf)
While the Bash tool can do similar things, it’s better to use the built-in tools as they provide a better user experience and make it easier to review tool calls and give permission.

# Instructions
 - If your command will create new directories or files, first use this tool to run `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location.
 - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes in your command (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")
 - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it. In particular, never prepend `cd <current-directory>` to a `git` command — `git` already operates on the current working tree, and the compound triggers a permission prompt.
 - You may specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). By default, your command will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
 - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.
 - For git commands:
  - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
  - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
  - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
 - Avoid unnecessary `sleep` commands:
  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.
  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
  - If you must poll an external process, use a check command (e.g. `gh run view`) rather than sleeping first.
  - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
 - When running `find`, search from `.` (or a specific path), not `/` — scanning the full filesystem can exhaust system resources on large trees.
 - When using `find -regex` with alternation, put the longest alternative first. Example: use `'.*\.\(tsx\|ts\)'` not `'.*\.\(ts\|tsx\)'` — the second form silently skips `.tsx` files.


# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'

   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:

   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed

   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)

)"

- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

Performs exact string replacements in files.

- You must use your `Read` tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file.

tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: ExitWorktree
tools.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

tools.name: NotebookEdit
tools.description:
Replaces, inserts, or deletes a single cell in a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb file).

Usage:
- You must use the Read tool on the notebook in this conversation before editing — this tool will fail otherwise.
- `notebook_path` must be an absolute path.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
IMPORTANT: WebFetch WILL FAIL for authenticated or private URLs. Before using this tool, check if the URL points to an authenticated service (e.g. Google Docs, Confluence, Jira, GitHub). If so, look for a specialized MCP tool that provides authenticated access.

- Fetches content from a specified URL and processes it using an AI model
- Takes a URL and a prompt as input
- Fetches the URL content, converts HTML to markdown
- Processes the content with the prompt using a small, fast model
- Returns the model's response about the content
- Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze web content

Usage notes:
  - IMPORTANT: If an MCP-provided web fetch tool is available, prefer using that tool instead of this one, as it may have fewer restrictions.
  - The URL must be a fully-formed valid URL
  - HTTP URLs will be automatically upgraded to HTTPS
  - localhost and other hostnames without a dot are not supported; for a local server, use curl via Bash
  - The prompt should describe what information you want to extract from the page
  - This tool is read-only and does not modify any files
  - Results may be summarized if the content is very large
  - Includes a self-cleaning cache (entries expire after 15 minutes) for faster responses when repeatedly accessing the same URL
  - When a URL redirects to a different host, the tool will inform you and provide the redirect URL in a special format. You should then make a new WebFetch request with the redirect URL to fetch the content.
  - For GitHub URLs, prefer using the gh CLI via Bash instead (e.g., gh pr view, gh issue view, gh api).

5	**Goal:** 构建符合 VDA 5050 工业标准的车队通信适配层（Fleet Protocol Adapter），向内通过统一抽象接口 `IVehicleAdapter` 衔接调度核心，向外通过标准 MQTT 协议接入异构移动机器人，实现标准化订单下发、状态归一化与逐段路权释放。
6	**Architecture:** 纯 C++ 核心库负责统一抽象接口定义、VDA 5050 JSON 报文编解码与 Order 构建（保持零 ROS、零 MQTT 依赖）；ROS 薄壳 `vda5050_gateway_node` 桥接 ROS 2 调度系统与外部 MQTT Broker；配套提供轻量 Python 虚拟小车进行端到端全链路自动化验收。

# VDA 5050 车队协议适配层与异构机器人接入实施计划

> REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use subagent-driven-development or executing-plans

**Goal:** 构建符合 VDA 5050 工业标准的车队通信适配层（Fleet Protocol Adapter），向内通过统一抽象接口 `IVehicleAdapter` 衔接调度核心，向外通过标准 MQTT 协议接入异构移动机器人，实现标准化订单下发、状态归一化与逐段路权释放。
**Architecture:** 纯 C++ 核心库负责统一抽象接口定义、VDA 5050 JSON 报文编解码与 Order 构建（保持零 ROS、零 MQTT 依赖）；ROS 薄壳 `vda5050_gateway_node` 桥接 ROS 2 调度系统与外部 MQTT Broker；配套提供轻量 Python 虚拟小车进行端到端全链路自动化验收。
**Tech Stack:** C++17, ROS 2 Jazzy, MQTT (mosquitto/libpaho), JSON, GoogleTest, Python 3
**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/vda5050_fleet_adapter.md`

## Global Constraints
1. 核心库 `amr_dispatcher_core` 保持**零 ROS 依赖、零 MQTT 依赖**，协议编解码与订单映射算法必须能在脱机单测（`ctest`）中毫秒级执行。
2. 遵循 TDD 规范：先写失败测试并确认红灯，再写最小实现使其变绿。
3. 严格遵循安全准则：MQTT 通信断开时，保留小车已持有的所有路网资源锁，杜绝后车追尾事故。

---

### Task 1: 核心库抽象车队控制接口与数据模型 (P0)

**Files:**
- Create: `src/amr_dispatcher_core/include/amr_dispatcher_core/fleet/vehicle_adapter_interface.hpp`
- Create: `src/amr_dispatcher_core/src/fleet/vehicle_adapter_interface.cpp`
- Modify: `src/amr_dispatcher_core/CMakeLists.txt`
- Create: `test/unit/test_vehicle_adapter_interface.cpp`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces: `IVehicleAdapter` 纯虚类、`VehicleOrder`、`VehicleNode`、`VehicleEdge`、`VehicleAction`、`VehicleStateReport` 结构体。
- Produces: `MockVehicleAdapter` 测试桩（实现内存单车状态维护与订单收发）。

- [ ] Step 1: 编写 `test_vehicle_adapter_interface.cpp`，测试基于 `MockVehicleAdapter` 的订单分发、状态更新与取消操作。
- [ ] Step 2: 运行测试确认红灯（头文件缺失）。
- [ ] Step 3: 实现 `vehicle_adapter_interface.hpp` 和 `vehicle_adapter_interface.cpp`。
- [ ] Step 4: 编译并运行单测，确认全部变绿（`ctest --test-dir build/core -R VehicleAdapter`）。
- [ ] Step 5: Git commit 提交改动。

---

### Task 2: 纯 C++ VDA 5050 报文序列化与反序列化引擎 (P1)

**Files:**
- Create: `src/amr_dispatcher_core/include/amr_dispatcher_core/fleet/vda5050_serializer.hpp`
- Create: `src/amr_dispatcher_core/src/fleet/vda5050_serializer.cpp`
- Modify: `src/amr_dispatcher_core/CMakeLists.txt`
- Create: `test/unit/test_vda5050_serializer.cpp`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces:
  - `std::string SerializeVda5050Order(const VehicleOrder& order, const std::string& version = "v2")`
  - `std::string SerializeVda5050InstantActions(const std::string& vehicle_id, const std::vector<VehicleAction>& actions)`
  - `std::optional<VehicleStateReport> DeserializeVda5050State(const std::string& json_str)`
  - `std::optional<std::string> DeserializeVda5050Connection(const std::string& json_str)` // "ONLINE", "CONNECTIONBROKEN"

- [ ] Step 1: 编写 `test_vda5050_serializer.cpp`，覆盖合规 JSON 报文解析、非法字段防护、NaN 坐标校验、以及 v2/v3 Topic 规范。
- [ ] Step 2: 运行测试确认红灯。
- [ ] Step 3: 在 `vda5050_serializer.hpp/cpp` 中实现轻量 JSON 编解码（纯标准库或轻量解析，零外部重依赖）。
- [ ] Step 4: 运行测试确认绿灯通过。
- [ ] Step 5: Git commit 提交改动。

---

### Task 3: 拓扑折线转 VDA 5050 订单构建引擎 `Vda5050OrderBuilder` (P1)

**Files:**
- Create: `src/amr_dispatcher_core/include/amr_dispatcher_core/fleet/vda5050_order_builder.hpp`
- Create: `src/amr_dispatcher_core/src/fleet/vda5050_order_builder.cpp`
- Modify: `src/amr_dispatcher_core/CMakeLists.txt`
- Create: `test/unit/test_vda5050_order_builder.cpp`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `StationCatalog`（含 road_nodes 与 polyline 边）、Dijkstra 路径节点序列、资源锁列表。
- Produces: `VehicleOrder BuildOrderFromPath(const std::string& vehicle_id, const std::string& mission_id, const std::vector<std::string>& path_node_ids, const catalog::StationCatalog& catalog, const std::unordered_set<std::string>& reserved_locks)`。
- Rule: 只有在 `reserved_locks` 存在的边和节点，设置 `released = true`（Base 区间）；未取得锁的设置为 `released = false`（Horizon 规划区间）。

- [ ] Step 1: 编写 `test_vda5050_order_builder.cpp`，验证 L 弯路径转换、Base/Horizon 分段放行标记及动作挂载。
- [ ] Step 2: 运行测试确认红灯。
- [ ] Step 3: 实现 `vda5050_order_builder.hpp/cpp`。
- [ ] Step 4: 运行单测确认全部绿灯（`ctest --test-dir build/core` 保持 100% 通过）。
- [ ] Step 5: Git commit 提交改动。

---

### Task 4: ROS 2 VDA 5050 MQTT 通信适配网关 `vda5050_gateway_node` (P2)

**Files:**
- Create: `src/amr_dispatcher_ros/include/amr_dispatcher_ros/vda5050_gateway_node.hpp`
- Create: `src/amr_dispatcher_ros/src/vda5050_gateway_node.cpp`
- Modify: `src/amr_dispatcher_ros/CMakeLists.txt`
- Modify: `launch/full_system.launch.py`

**Interfaces:**
- 负责与外部 MQTT Broker 通信：
  - 订阅 `uagv/v2/+/+/state`，解析后转换为 ROS 2 话题 `/fleet/{vehicle_id}/state` 与位姿 `/odom`。
  - 订阅 `uagv/v2/+/+/connection`，检测 LWT 遗嘱断链，通知调度安全门。
  - 监听内部调度下发，生成并发布 `uagv/v2/{manufacturer}/{serialNumber}/order`。
- 提供启动参数：`use_vda5050`（默认 false），`mqtt_broker_host`（默认 "127.0.0.1"），`mqtt_port`（默认 1883）。

- [ ] Step 1: 在 `amr_dispatcher_ros/CMakeLists.txt` 中配置编译目标与依赖。
- [ ] Step 2: 实现 `vda5050_gateway_node` 核心收发逻辑与 MQTT 客户端封装。
- [ ] Step 3: 更新 `full_system.launch.py`，支持一键拉起 VDA 5050 网关。
- [ ] Step 4: 容器内编译验证通过。
- [ ] Step 5: Git commit 提交改动。

---

### Task 5: 逐段路权动态释放与断链安全守卫 (P3)

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/amr_dispatcher_core/src/workflow/traffic_planning.cpp`
- Modify: `src/amr_dispatcher_ros/src/dispatcher_node.cpp`
- Create: `test/unit/test_dynamic_unlocking.cpp`

**Interfaces:**
- Rule 1 (动态解锁): 当收到小车上报 `lastNodeId` 已经跨越 node_A 进入 edge_AB 时，自动调用 `ResourceTable` 释放已离开的路网节点与边锁，唤醒等待后车。
- Rule 2 (断链安全): 当小车 connection 离线时，保留其持有锁，挂起派发并触发软看门狗告警。

- [ ] Step 1: 编写单测验证车辆沿折线推进时逐段释放旧锁逻辑。
- [ ] Step 2: 运行单测确认红灯。
- [ ] Step 3: 在 `dispatcher_node` 中接入 VDA 5050 状态流，打通动态解锁与断链保护。
- [ ] Step 4: 运行单测确认全部变绿。
- [ ] Step 5: Git commit 提交改动。

---

### Task 6: Python 虚拟小车模拟器与端到端联合验收 (P2/P3)

**Files:**
- Create: `scripts/mock_vda5050_vehicle.py`

  1. 启动轻量 Mosquitto MQTT Broker；

  3. 启动 `mock_vda5050_vehicle.py`；
  4. 提单下发，验证 MQTT 收到合法 VDA 5050 Order；
  5. 验证小车沿折线运动、中心端逐段解锁、最终到达完成；
  6. 验证模拟断链场景下，锁不被非法释放。

- [ ] Step 1: 编写 `mock_vda5050_vehicle.py` 仿真脚本。

1	#pragma once

13	namespace amr_dispatcher_core::fleet {
14	
15	// Vda5050OrderBuilder 默认配置。
16	struct Vda5050OrderBuilderConfig {
17	  double default_max_speed_mps = 1.0;
18	  std::string default_map_id = "map";
19	};
20	
21	// 将调度选出的拓扑路径节点序列转换为标准 VehicleOrder（Spec §4.2 / §5）。
22	//
23	// 参数:
24	//   - vehicle_id: 目标小车 ID
25	//   - mission_id: 业务任务 ID（作为 order_id，保证整单可寻址）
26	//   - order_update_id: 订单更新版本号
27	//   - path_node_ids: Dijkstra 产出的节点 ID 序列（例如 ["station_A", "rn_1", "station_B"]）
28	//   - catalog: 当前生效的路网拓扑目录（stations + road_nodes + 带 polyline 的 edges）
29	//   - reserved_locks: 本单在 ResourceTable 中实际持有的资源集合（RouteNodeId / RouteEdgeId）。
30	//     注意：调用方必须只传入「当前 mission 名下」已 Reserve 成功的锁，严禁传入全局锁表快照——
31	//     否则其他车辆的锁会被误判为本单已放行，向小车下发未获路权的 released=true 边（违反 Spec §5.1）。
32	//   - terminal_actions: 挂载在终点站点的动作（取货/卸货/充电等）
33	//   - config: 默认速度与地图 ID 配置

Now, where does the dispatcher know the vehicle's order path? At dispatch, `route_locks` = PlanMissionRouteLocks(catalog, from, to) — a station path with intersection locks. The path_node_ids order used in the lock list is `BuildLockIds(path, true)` = [node(path0), node(path1), ..., node(pathN), edge(path0,path1), ..., edge(pathN-1,pathN)] — note nodes all first, then edges! Design: the unlock decision function should take:

And return the lock ids to release.

Sequence id semantics: in VehicleOrder, nodes are even: node i has sequence_id = 2*i. Edges occupy odd slot: edge between node i and i+1 has sequence_id2*i+1. So confirmed_last_node_sequence_id = 2*k means the vehicle is ON node path[k]. If lastNodeId = path[k]:
- vehicle has passed nodes path[0..k-1] → release node locks route_node:path[0..k-1]
- vehicle has passed edges (0→1), ..., (k-2→k-1) → release those edge locks
- keep: node path[k] (currently occupied), edge (k→k+1) (currently traversing), nodes path[k+1..] and edges (k+1→k+2)...

At k=0: nothing released (vehicle at start).
At k=1: release node path[0]; edge(0→1) is currently traversed → KEEP locked.
At k=2: release node path[0], edge(0→1), node path[1]; keep edge(1→2) and node path[2].

That matches the task's footprint rule: "node currently occupied + edge currently traversed remain locked."

- confirmed_last_node_id empty → release nothing.

namespace amr_dispatcher_core::workflow {

// 逐段动态解锁（Spec §5.3）：依据车辆确认推进的 lastNodeId 计算身后已脱离、可安全释放的锁。
//
// 足迹规则（保守）：lastNodeId = path[k]（sequence_id == 2k校验通过）时，
//   - 车辆已物理通过 nodes path[0..k-1] 与 edges (0→1)..(k-2→k-1) →可释放；
//   - 车尾可能仍压在入边 edge(k-1→k) 上 → 保留；
//   - 当前占位节点 path[k] → 保留；
//   - 可能即将驶入的出边 edge(k→k+1) → 保留；
//   - 全部前方资源 → 保留。
// k == 0（车辆仍在起点）→ 不释放任何锁。
// lastNodeId 为空/不在路径中/sequence 不符 → 判定为不确定，不释放任何锁（保守）。
// 仅释放 owner == owner_mission_id 的锁：他人锁（含 traffic_block 与他车任务）绝不触碰。
struct TrailingUnlockDecision {
  bool position_confirmed = false;   // lastNodeId 与 sequence校验通过且命中路径
  std::vector<std::string> lock_ids_to_release;  // 已按 owner 过滤
  std::string message;
};

TrailingUnlockDecision PlanTrailingUnlock(
    const std::vector<std::string>& order_path_node_ids,
    const std::string& confirmed_last_node_id,
    std::uint32_t confirmed_last_node_sequence_id,
    const std::string& owner_mission_id,
    const RouteLockMap& route_locks);

// 断链安全守卫（Spec §5.2）：铁律编码——离线或状态陈旧时一律保留全部锁，
// 绝不释放；仅离线时额外拦截新派发。retain_locks 恒为 true（铁律不可配置）。
struct VehicleLinkGuardDecision {
  bool retain_locks = true; // 铁律：无条件保留
  bool block_new_dispatch = false; //离线时 true
  std::string warning;             // 需上层打印的告警（空 = 无需告警）
};
VehicleLinkGuardDecision EvaluateVehicleLinkGuard(bool vehicle_online,
                                                  bool state_report_stale);
}

  const auto decision = amr_dispatcher_core::workflow::PlanTrailingUnlock(
      path_it->second, report->last_node_id, report->last_node_sequence_id, report->order_id, lock_owners);

}

10	// 未命中返回 nullptr（调用方据此判定非法路径）。
11	const void* FindNodeCoords(const catalog::StationCatalog& catalog,
12	                           const std::string& node_id,
13	                           double* x,
14	                           double* y,
15	                           double* yaw) {

37	const catalog::CatalogStationEdge* FindCatalogEdge(const catalog::StationCatalog& catalog,
38	                                                   const std::string& start,
39	                                                   const std::string& end,
40	                                                   bool* traversed_backward) {
41	  for (const auto& edge : catalog.edges) {
42	    if (edge.from == start && edge.to == end) {
43	      *traversed_backward = false;
44	      return &edge;
45	    }
46	    if (edge.bidirectional && edge.to == start && edge.from == end) {
47	      *traversed_backward = true;
48	      return &edge;
49	    }
50	  }
51	  return nullptr;
52	}

54	// 把 (x, y) 折线点转为带航向的轨迹点：每点航向取到下一点方向，末点沿用前段方向。
55	std::vector<VehicleTrajectoryPoint> BuildTrajectory(
56	    const std::vector<std::pair<double, double>>& points) {
57	  std::vector<VehicleTrajectoryPoint> trajectory;
58	  trajectory.reserve(points.size());
59	  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < points.size(); ++i) {
60	    VehicleTrajectoryPoint point;
61	    point.x = points[i].first;
62	    point.y = points[i].second;
63	    if (points.size() == 1) {
64	      point.yaw = 0.0;
65	    } else if (i + 1 < points.size()) {
66	      point.yaw = std::atan2(points[i + 1].second - points[i].second,
67	                             points[i + 1].first - points[i].first);
68	    } else {
69	      point.yaw = trajectory.back().yaw;  // 末点沿用上一段航向
70	    }
71	    trajectory.push_back(point);
72	  }

78	                                                             double start_y,

81	  std::vector<VehicleTrajectoryPoint> trajectory(2);
82	  const double yaw = std::atan2(end_y - start_y, end_x - start_x);
83	  trajectory[0].x = start_x;
84	  trajectory[0].y = start_y;
85	  trajectory[0].yaw = yaw;
86	  trajectory[1].x = end_x;

94	std::optional<VehicleOrder> BuildVda5050OrderFromPath(
95	    const std::string& vehicle_id,
96	    const std::string& mission_id,
97	    const uint32_t order_update_id,
98	    const std::vector<std::string>& path_node_ids,
99	    const catalog::StationCatalog& catalog,
100	    const std::unordered_set<std::string>& reserved_locks,
101	    const std::vector<VehicleAction>& terminal_actions,
102	    const Vda5050OrderBuilderConfig& config) {
103	  if (path_node_ids.empty()) {
104	    return std::nullopt;
105	  }
106	
107	  const std::size_t node_count = path_node_ids.size();
108	
109	  // 1. 提取所有节点坐标；任一节点缺失即整单作废（防止小车驶向未定义坐标）。
110	  std::vector<double> xs(node_count);
111	  std::vector<double> ys(node_count);
112	  std::vector<double> yaws(node_count);
113	  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < node_count; ++i) {
114	    if (FindNodeCoords(catalog, path_node_ids[i], &xs[i], &ys[i], &yaws[i]) == nullptr) {
115	      return std::nullopt;
116	    }
117	  }
118	
119	  // 2. 原始放行判定（仅看锁，尚未做协议一致性拉平）。
120	  const std::size_t edge_count = node_count - 1;
121	  std::vector<bool> node_raw(node_count, false);
122	  std::vector<bool> edge_raw(edge_count, false);
123	  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < node_count; ++i) {
124	    node_raw[i] = reserved_locks.count(dispatcher::ResourceTable::RouteNodeId(
125	                      path_node_ids[i])) > 0;
126	  }
127	  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < edge_count; ++i) {
128	    const auto edge_id = dispatcher::ResourceTable::RouteEdgeId(path_node_ids[i],
129	                                                                path_node_ids[i + 1]);
130	    // 边锁存在且两端节点均已获路权
131	    edge_raw[i] = reserved_locks.count(edge_id) > 0 && node_raw[i] && node_raw[i + 1];
132	  }
133	
134	  // 3. 协议一致性拉平：按 node0 -> edge0 -> node1 -> edge1 ... 的行驶顺序遍历，
135	  //    一旦出现 released = false（Horizon 区间），其后所有节点与边一律为 false
136	  //    （VDA 5050 规定 Horizon 之后不得再出现 Base 区间）。
137	  std::vector<bool> node_released(node_count, false);
138	  std::vector<bool> edge_released(edge_count, false);
139	  bool horizon_started = false;
140	  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < node_count; ++i) {
141	    node_released[i] = !horizon_started && node_raw[i];
142	    horizon_started = horizon_started || !node_released[i];
143	    if (i + 1 < node_count) {
144	      edge_released[i] = !horizon_started && edge_raw[i];
145	      horizon_started = horizon_started || !edge_released[i];
146	    }
147	  }
148	
149	  // 4. 组装订单：sequence_id 取 VDA 5050 规范的偶数序列 0, 2, 4 ...
150	  VehicleOrder order;
151	  order.order_id = mission_id;
152	  order.order_update_id = order_update_id;
153	  order.vehicle_id = vehicle_id;
154	  order.nodes.reserve(node_count);
155	  order.edges.reserve(edge_count);
156	
157	  const std::size_t last_index = node_count - 1;
158	  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < node_count; ++i) {
159	    VehicleNode node;
160	    node.node_id = path_node_ids[i];
161	    node.sequence_id = static_cast<uint32_t>(i * 2);
162	    node.x = xs[i];
163	    node.y = ys[i];
164	    node.yaw = yaws[i];
165	    node.released = node_released[i];
166	    if (i == last_index) {
167	      node.actions = terminal_actions;  // 终点动作挂载
168	    }
169	    order.nodes.push_back(std::move(node));
170	
171	    if (i + 1 < node_count) {
172	      VehicleEdge edge;
173	      edge.start_node_id = path_node_ids[i];
174	      edge.end_node_id = path_node_ids[i + 1];
175	      edge.edge_id = dispatcher::ResourceTable::RouteEdgeId(edge.start_node_id,
176	                                                            edge.end_node_id);
177	      edge.released = edge_released[i];
178	      edge.max_speed = config.default_max_speed_mps;
179	
180	      bool traversed_backward = false;
181	      const auto* catalog_edge =
182	          FindCatalogEdge(catalog, edge.start_node_id, edge.end_node_id, &traversed_backward);
183	      // 折线必须至少 2 个点才构成合法轨迹段；单点折线视同缺失，走直线兜底，
184	      // 避免向小车下发只有一个控制点的无效 VDA 5050 轨迹。
185	      if (catalog_edge != nullptr && catalog_edge->polyline.size() >= 2) {
186	        auto points = catalog_edge->polyline;
187	        if (traversed_backward) {
188	          std::reverse(points.begin(), points.end());  // 反向行驶：折线按行驶方向反转
189	        }
190	        edge.polyline = BuildTrajectory(points);
191	      } else {
192	        edge.polyline = BuildStraightLineFallback(xs[i], ys[i], xs[i + 1], ys[i + 1]);
193	      }
194	
195	      order.edges.push_back(std::move(edge));
196	    }
197	  }
198	
199	  return order;
200	}

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a given bash command and returns its output.

The working directory persists between commands, but shell state does not. The shell environment is initialized from the user's profile (bash or zsh).

IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user:

 - Read files: Use Read (NOT cat/head/tail)
 - Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)
 - Write files: Use Write (NOT echo >/cat <<EOF)
 - Communication: Output text directly (NOT echo/printf)
While the Bash tool can do similar things, it’s better to use the built-in tools as they provide a better user experience and make it easier to review tool calls and give permission.

# Instructions
 - If your command will create new directories or files, first use this tool to run `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location.
 - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes in your command (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")
 - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it. In particular, never prepend `cd <current-directory>` to a `git` command — `git` already operates on the current working tree, and the compound triggers a permission prompt.
 - You may specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). By default, your command will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
 - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.
 - For git commands:
  - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
  - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
  - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
 - Avoid unnecessary `sleep` commands:
  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.
  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
  - If you must poll an external process, use a check command (e.g. `gh run view`) rather than sleeping first.
  - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
 - When running `find`, search from `.` (or a specific path), not `/` — scanning the full filesystem can exhaust system resources on large trees.
 - When using `find -regex` with alternation, put the longest alternative first. Example: use `'.*\.\(tsx\|ts\)'` not `'.*\.\(ts\|tsx\)'` — the second form silently skips `.tsx` files.


# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: ExitWorktree
tools.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

tools.name: NotebookEdit
tools.description:
Replaces, inserts, or deletes a single cell in a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb file).

Usage:
- You must use the Read tool on the notebook in this conversation before editing — this tool will fail otherwise.
- `notebook_path` must be an absolute path.
- `cell_id` is the `id` attribute shown in the Read tool's `<cell id="...">` output. It is required for `replace` and `delete`.
- `edit_mode` defaults to `replace`. Use `insert` to add a new cell after the cell with the given `cell_id` (or at the beginning of the notebook if `cell_id` is omitted) — `cell_type` is required when inserting. Use `delete` to remove the cell.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID ("name@team") or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID ("name@team") or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
IMPORTANT: WebFetch WILL FAIL for authenticated or private URLs. Before using this tool, check if the URL points to an authenticated service (e.g. Google Docs, Confluence, Jira, GitHub). If so, look for a specialized MCP tool that provides authenticated access.

- Fetches content from a specified URL and processes it using an AI model
- Takes a URL and a prompt as input
- Fetches the URL content, converts HTML to markdown
- Processes the content with the prompt using a small, fast model
- Returns the model's response about the content
- Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze web content

Usage notes:
  - IMPORTANT: If an MCP-provided web fetch tool is available, prefer using that tool instead of this one, as it may have fewer restrictions.
  - The URL must be a fully-formed valid URL
  - HTTP URLs will be automatically upgraded to HTTPS
  - localhost and other hostnames without a dot are not supported; for a local server, use curl via Bash
  - The prompt should describe what information you want to extract from the page
  - This tool is read-only and does not modify any files
  - Results may be summarized if the content is very large
  - Includes a self-cleaning cache (entries expire after 15 minutes) for faster responses when repeatedly accessing the same URL
  - When a URL redirects to a different host, the tool will inform you and provide the redirect URL in a special format. You should then make a new WebFetch request with the redirect URL to fetch the content.
  - For GitHub URLs, prefer using the gh CLI via Bash instead (e.g., gh pr view, gh issue view, gh api).

tools.name: WebSearch
tools.description:
- Allows Claude to search the web and use the results to inform responses
- Provides up-to-date information for current events and recent data
- Returns search result information formatted as search result blocks, including links as markdown hyperlinks
- Use this tool for accessing information beyond Claude's knowledge cutoff
- Searches are performed automatically within a single API call

CRITICAL REQUIREMENT - You MUST follow this:
  - After answering the user's question, you MUST include a "Sources:" section at the end of your response
  - In the Sources section, list all relevant URLs from the search results as markdown hyperlinks: [Title](URL)
  - This is MANDATORY - never skip including sources in your response
  - Example format:

    [Your answer here]

    Sources:
    - [Source Title 1](https://example.com/1)
    - [Source Title 2](https://example.com/2)

Usage notes:
  - Domain filtering is supported to include or block specific websites
  - Web search is only available in the US

IMPORTANT - Use the correct year in search queries:
  - The current month is October 2026. You MUST use this year when searching for recent information, documentation, or current events.
  - Example: If the user asks for "latest React docs", search for "React documentation" with the current year, NOT last year
